about: Part of the reference catalogue: designs from one published source, for testing that software reproduces them.
Fries and Hunter (1980) define the minimum-aberration criterion for 2^(k-p) fractional factorials: of the
designs of maximum resolution, the one with the fewest words of minimum length in its defining relation. designs:
Table 1's three 2^(7-2) designs of resolution IV, with their generators, defining relations, word length patterns
and aliased two-factor interactions, and the worked example of Section 4; and Table 2's maximum resolution R_max
for 48 choices of k and p. Each expected item has its printed text, where it is printed (a page and a quotation)
and a check, or manual: the reason it is not recomputed. not_captured lists what was left out.

source.rights: The article is protected by copyright and is not reproduced here; read it through its DOI. This file holds facts it reports (numbers, design matrices, data) and short quotations that locate each one, for citation and for checking software. The MIT licence of process-improve does not extend to them.

designs.name: fries-hunter-table-2-maximum-resolution
designs.title: The maximum resolution R_max of a 2^(k-p) design for k = 5 to 14 factors and p = 2 to 10 generators

design.details: 48 choices of k and p, 8 to 4096 runs

designs.notes: An asterisk marks a row whose bound (3) exceeds R_max. 42 of the 48 rows hold; six do not, each with its reason. A 2^(k-p) design of resolution R is a binary linear [k, p] code of minimum distance R (its words are the defining relation's), which is how the search reaching each R_max is set up: the base factors are interchangeable, so one generator's letters can be fixed.
